subject.title: Deny same-provider cross-context message sends by default

question: Should OpenClaw make same-provider cross-context message sends fail closed by default in this release, requiring existing intentional forwarding deployments to opt back in?
rationale: The patch narrows a real outbound authorization risk, but it deliberately changes shipped behavior and can stop legitimate bridge workflows; code review cannot choose that security-versus-upgrade policy on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed after proof
options.body: Accept the safer default after exact-head Telegram proof and explicit upgrade communication for operators who must set `allowWithinProvider=true`.

options.title: Preserve the current default
options.body: Keep permissive same-provider forwarding as the default and continue requiring security-conscious deployments to set the existing option to false.

options.title: Pause the rollout
options.body: Hold the PR until broader channel-specific transport proof or a staged migration plan reduces the compatibility uncertainty.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the safer default after exact-head Telegram proof and explicit upgrade communication for operators who must set `allowWithinProvider=true`.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available recent history signal on the shared outbound-policy surface where the permanent default is enforced.
